note: Confirmed extraction errors, kept out of precision.json because the stratified sampling rule (first N per repo) excludes these rows. They are tracked so a sampling change cannot hide them.
cause: the path is named in one sentence of the turn while the agent's actual subject is a different file in another sentence

cases.note: turn reviews main.py; the dispatcher.py path matched elsewhere in the message
cases.diagnosis: DIAGNOSED, NOT FIXED. Both cases are one defect: the agent hypothesises about a file, states an intent, and shows the open command in a fenced block -- and the fenced command is the only thing naming a path, so the tracker promoted a shown command to an executed action. 'navigate to X' matched first; the fence's 'open X' matched second and won on last-write. A fix was implemented and measured, then reverted. Stripping fenced blocks before pattern matching cost 48% of the measured supersession signal (keys_reasserted 77 -> 40, turns_retired 161 -> 124 at n=40) because in this corpus the fence IS how the agent opens a file -- and it did not even fix these cases: one transcript still extracted dispatcher.py and the other extracted nothing at all. Dropping the intent verbs is free (77 -> 78) but fixes nothing on its own. The blocker is that the expected value in these labels was itself produced by the same pattern, so correcting them is a re-labelling exercise, not a regex change.
